findings.content: Intermediate creation in `_extra_body.assign` allows creating a dict-shaped `tools` value when the request has no tools. The list-index guard only applies when `target` is already a list, but the `key not in target` branch creates `{}` for missing `tools` because `strict_flag` clears `protected`. A dotted `tools.0.strict` key therefore silently builds `body["tools"]={"0":{"strict":...}}` instead of raising invalid tool index.
findings.trigger: Configure connection `options.extra_body` with `{"tools.0.strict": true}` (or `tools.0.function.strict`) and call `encode_request` for a request with `request.tools == []`, so `body` has no `tools` list.
findings.consequence: encode_request returns a malformed provider body where `tools` is a dict `{"0": {"strict": true}}` instead of a list. The request bypasses the intended invalid-index rejection and strict validation, causing a downstream provider rejection, wasted inference call, or unexpected payload shape.

assessment.explanation: Required behavior: `tools.<index>.strict` extra_body keys must refer to an existing tool list entry; otherwise `_extra_body` must raise invalid tool index and must not fabricate a dict-shaped `tools` value. This is shown by the list guard that rejects non-digit or out-of-range indices when target is already a list, and by `encode_request` creating `body["tools"]` only as a list when `request.tools` is non-empty. Actual behavior: with `request.tools==[]` body has no `tools`, `strict_flag` clears `protected` for `tools.0.strict`, so the intermediate-creation branch creates `body["tools"]={}` then `{"0":{}}` then sets `strict`, yielding `{"0":{"strict":true}}` dict. Counterevidence checked: strict boolean-type check remains but does not validate index; final `_extra_body` checks cover only `n`, `thinking`, and budget, with no tools-shape validation or recovery path; `PROTECTED` block is explicitly disabled for this path, so no alternative guard rejects it. Therefore confirmed.
assessment.cause: The `else` intermediate branch at lines 109-112 creates `{}` for any missing dict key when `protected` is False, without validating tool-index references. Because `strict_flag` clears `protected` for `tools.<digit>.strict` / `tools.<digit>.function.strict`, a missing `body["tools"]` is fabricated as a dict, and the subsequent `"0"` part is then handled as a dict key, so the list-index guard at lines 93-95 never applies.
assessment.trigger: Configure `options.extra_body` with `{"tools.0.strict": true}` (or `tools.0.function.strict`) and call `encode_request` for a request with `request.tools==[]`, so `body` has no `tools` list before `_extra_body`.
assessment.consequence: encode_request returns a malformed provider body with `body["tools"]=={"0":{"strict":...}}` dict instead of a list. It bypasses the intended invalid-index rejection and is returned to the HTTP sender with no later tools-shape check, causing downstream provider rejection, wasted inference call, or unexpected payload shape.

def assign(parts, value):
        dotted = ".".join(parts)
        strict_flag = (len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "tools" and parts[1].isdigit() and parts[2] == "strict") or (

        protected = parts[0] in PROTECTED and not strict_flag

findings.content: RepoSettings.valid_rules claims rules.rules entries require path, rule and merge_system_rule fields, but the guard only rejects non-dicts and extra keys. An entry such as {'path': 'x'} has set(entry) - allowed == empty and therefore passes validation.
findings.trigger: Validate review configuration with rules={'rules': [{'path': 'src/'}]} missing rule and merge_system_rule via settings.load or RepoSettings.model_validate.
findings.consequence: A rule entry missing required fields passes the explicit rules.rules validation instead of being rejected, so an incomplete configuration is forwarded to planning._rule_layer rather than raising the stated ValueError.

assessment.explanation: Required behavior per settings.py message is that rules.rules entries require path, rule and merge_system_rule fields, i.e. missing fields must raise ValueError. Actual behavior: guard only rejects non-dicts and extra keys via set(entry)-allowed, so {'path':'x'} has empty difference and passes, then returns planning._rule_layer(value). Counterevidence checked: _rule_layer also uses entry.get with defaults and only validates types of defaulted values, so it normalizes missing fields instead of rejecting; no other guard enforces presence. Therefore mismatch confirmed.
assessment.cause: Guard at valid_rules only tests not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) - allowed, omitting the missing-keys test allowed - set(entry), so a subset dict yields empty difference and passes.
assessment.trigger: Validate rules={'rules':[{'path':'src/'}]} via RepoSettings.model_validate or settings.load; include/exclude default to [] so list checks pass and per-entry check is reached with subset dict.
assessment.consequence: Entry {'path':'x'} passes the explicit rules.rules validation instead of raising the stated ValueError and is forwarded to planning._rule_layer where .get defaults normalize it to rule='' and merge_system_rule=False.
assessment.history_explanation: history and prior_candidates are empty; no established finding matches this validator defect, so relationship is new.
assessment.changed_conditions: No prior assessment; current revision retains the extra-keys-only check.

findings.content: Previous-history IDs are used without per-record validation: history_findings() only checks schema_version and list length, then scan() builds previous_ids with old["id"]. A history record without "id" passes validation and crashes the comprehension.
findings.existing_code:

findings.trigger: Call scan() with previous={"schema_version": "mortis.security/v1", "findings": [{}]} or any record missing "id". history_findings() returns it because it only validates that findings is a list.
findings.consequence: Unhandled KeyError escapes scan() instead of a ValueError or structured security report. The snapshot, trivy, analysis, assessment and verification stages are abandoned, no grade/coverage is returned, and the caller cannot distinguish corrupt history from an infrastructure failure.

assessment.explanation: Required behavior: invalid previous history should be rejected with ValueError as history_findings does for bad schema_version/non-list/oversize, and scan callers expect entries usable as dicts with id. Actual behavior: with previous={'schema_version':'mortis.security/v1','findings':[{}]}, history_findings returns [{}] via json.loads(json.dumps(findings)), secret_rules tolerates {} via finding.get, then scan executes previous_ids={old["id"]:old for old in previous_findings} which raises KeyError for missing id. Counterevidence checked: no per-record isinstance/id guard in history_findings; no guard before previous_ids; trivy try/except is before this line and its failure path also spreads previous_findings, so it does not recover this crash. Therefore confirmed as same defect.
assessment.cause: history_findings() only validates schema_version and that findings is a list with len<=10000, then returns json round-trip without per-record validation; scan() then unconditionally dereferences old["id"].
assessment.trigger: Call scan() with previous={"schema_version":"mortis.security/v1","findings":[{}]} or any dict record without string id; accepted by history_findings then dereferenced at previous_ids.
assessment.consequence: Malformed history with {} passes validation then raises unhandled KeyError at previous_ids construction, aborting scan() outside ValueError validation and outside trivy-failure structured-report path, so no grade/coverage/stages are returned.

findings.content: OpenAI Chat decoding iterates message.get("tool_calls", []) directly. That default only covers a missing key. When a provider returns explicit JSON null ("tool_calls": null, common for OpenAI-compatible endpoints when no tools are called), message.get returns None and iteration raises TypeError, which is converted to malformed_response. Nearby optional fields (content, reasoning_content/details) explicitly allow None, but tool_calls does not.
findings.trigger: Provider returns choices[0].message as {"content": "hi", "tool_calls": None} with finish_reason "stop" for protocol "openai".
findings.consequence: A valid Chat Completions response with explicit null tool_calls is rejected as malformed_response. The caller receives InferenceError malformed_response instead of a usable Response, wasting the request, token budget and retry/time budget and potentially failing review/scan stages.

assessment.explanation: Required behavior: explicit null for optional Chat message fields means absent. This is shown by content handling that skips when None and reasoning_content/details handling that explicitly allows None, and by stop=="stop" being defined as complete so empty calls with content should decode to Response. Actual behavior: `for call in message.get("tool_calls", []):` returns None when wire value is null, `for ... in None` raises TypeError, which the broad handler converts to malformed_response. Counterevidence checked: no isinstance/None guard for tool_calls, no alternative recovery; wire dict flows unfiltered from post_json to decode_response via send. Therefore confirmed.
assessment.cause: OpenAI Chat branch iterates `message.get("tool_calls", [])` directly. The default only applies when the key is missing; explicit JSON null returns None, which is not iterable. No None-guard or isinstance check precedes iteration, unlike nearby optional fields.
assessment.trigger: Provider returns choices[0].message as {"content":"hi","tool_calls":None} with finish_reason "stop" for protocol "openai"; wire JSON null survives post_json and reaches decode_response as None.
assessment.consequence: A valid Chat Completions response with explicit `"tool_calls": null` and `finish_reason "stop"` raises TypeError inside the try and is converted to InferenceError malformed_response instead of returning Response with empty tool_calls. Caller loses a usable response and wastes request/budget.
assessment.history_explanation: history_1 concerns _extra_body intermediate creation fabricating dict-shaped body["tools"] at lines 109-113, a different cause, location, trigger and fix. No established finding concerns OpenAI decode tool_calls null handling, so relationship is new.
assessment.changed_conditions: No prior established finding for this cause; assessed directly at current revision using supplied llm_http.py. No ownership or recovery-contract change needed to distinguish it.

Actual behavior: for path `dir/file` where `dir` is a regular file, `os.open(part, O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW)` raises NotADirectoryError/ENOTDIR, a subclass of OSError distinct from FileNotFoundError, so it falls to `except OSError: raise ValueError(cannot be read safely...)` and aborts snapshot. Counterevidence checked: only FileNotFoundError returns None; no NotADirectoryError/ENOTDIR guard; ELOOP for true symlink still needs ValueError but ENOTDIR does not; caller has None recovery path but it is unreachable for ENOTDIR. Therefore confirmed.

assessment.changed_conditions: No prior findings or candidates to compare; assessed at current revision.
assessment.consequence: Malformed entry passes validation then crashes downstream dict dereferences with AttributeError/TypeError/KeyError instead of ValueError, aborting scan() outside the trivy-failure structured-report path.
assessment.explanation: Required behavior: invalid previous history should raise ValueError (as history_findings does for bad schema_version/non-list/oversize with message 'Previous security finding history is invalid or exceeds 10000 records'), and scan callers expect validated dict entries. Actual behavior: with previous={'schema_version':'mortis.security/v1','findings':[None]}, history_findings returns [None] via json.loads(json.dumps(findings)). Downstream then unconditionally treats entries as dicts: secret_rules does finding.get("evidence") and finding["evidence"], scan builds {old["id"]:old} and {old.get("fingerprint"):old} and {**old}. None causes AttributeError on .get, TypeError on old["id"]/{**old}. Counterevidence checked: no per-entry isinstance guard in history_findings; no dict-entry guard in secret_rules/finding_evidence/observe paths; trivy try/except starts after secret_rules/previous_findings use and trivy-failure path itself spreads previous_findings, so it does not recover. Truthy non-dict previous sub-claim crashes earlier at repository check, but [None] case alone establishes mismatch. Therefore confirmed. Suggestion only adds isinstance(row,dict) check so it fixes non-dict crash but leaves dict-missing-id/fingerprint KeyError (e.g. {} fails old["id"]), so incomplete.

result.narrative: The snapshot presents Mortis Engine as a local Python package with a mortis command line tool and supporting library modules. Visible excerpts describe review of local Git revisions, verification of reported evidence against pinned revisions, background summaries, candidate assessment, and offline security scanning. Supporting areas include saved connection profiles, provider transports, local history storage, immutable reports, and an optional isolated parser for structural context. The supplied diff creates all listed paths as new files and the excerpts are truncated with limited context enabled, so only initial lines and brief documentation strings are visible and complete behavior cannot be determined.

groups.title: Project packaging and documentation
groups.description: These files define the installable project, license terms, ignore rules, automation workflow, overview documentation, and planning notes. Visible excerpts name the package version, Python requirements, install tooling, and main branch workflow, but all file bodies are truncated so complete settings remain unseen.

groups.title: Command line entry and commands
groups.description: This set provides the program entry, argument parsing, and terminal commands for review, scan, saved runs, connection setup, findings triage, followup assessments, and report export. Excerpts show separation between execution options, profile selection, progress display, and output handling, with details limited to truncated beginnings.

groups.title: Connection transport and safety helpers
groups.description: These modules handle saved connection profiles, provider presets, endpoint validation, direct HTTP protocols, pooled dispatch, request admission slots, and shared inference schemas. Excerpts indicate credential handling, redaction rules, bounded protocols, and destination hashing, but truncation prevents full review of logic.

groups.title: Local history and operation entry points
groups.description: This group stores private local run history, immutable task inputs, finding decisions, markdown presentation, candidate scoped assessment retries, and standalone operation functions. Excerpts describe exact input handling and offline report rendering, with remaining behavior hidden by truncation.

groups.title: Pinned review preparation and orchestration
groups.description: These review modules prepare immutable Git inputs without checkout, plan deterministic assignments, read pinned objects, apply configuration limits, and execute bounded workflows. Excerpts note credential free Git access and exclusion handling, with full flow only partially visible due to truncated excerpts.

groups.title: Review evidence validation and reporting stages
groups.description: This set covers finding contracts, context sanitization, independent adjudication, evidence selection, verification against original and current revisions, background generation, summaries, reporting scopes, and cancellation signaling. Excerpts show strict models and source only quotes, with truncated prompts limiting complete description.

groups.title: Isolated structural code context
groups.description: The code graph package offers optional exact revision structural facts from a disposable containerized parser, with contracts, syntax capabilities, supplied bytes parsing, transport without host mounts, and validation against source bytes. Excerpts show size limits and language tables, with implementation largely truncated.

groups.title: Offline security analysis workflow
groups.description: These modules implement static security analysis with inert snapshots, scanner normalization, strict response validation, payload references, policy supplements, offline enforcement, advisory lookup, and local workflow service. Excerpts indicate offline source analysis and evidence handling, with most logic truncated.

groups.title: Review test helpers and fixtures
groups.description: The test area contains package markers, a temporary repository fixture, Git helper functions for isolated commits, and a partial review JSON example.
